title: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefosai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefosai (or Kabsa, Kabsoy, Kofsai, Kefutzai).

His beginnings reach back to the generation of Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Akiva. As in [Tosefta Mikvaot 6:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Mikvaot.6.1), which relates an incident involving Rabban Gamliel and Onkelos the convert, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kofsai said (in the Zuckermandel Tosefta: ben Kevusai): ‘I was with them, and Rabban Gamliel immersed only in the sea.’

In [Avodah Zarah 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.32a.6), Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefosai. In [Bekhorot 35b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.35b), Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefosai disagrees with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and Rabbi Yose.

In [Tosefta Demai 1:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Demai_(Lieberman).1.14) (1:10 in Hyman), and in [Jerusalem Talmud Demai 3:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Demai.3.4.7), Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kofsai (in the Yerushalmi the reading is Kabsoy) says: ‘All my days I read this verse—and I found it only in the treasury of Yavneh.’ In [Bekhorot 39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.39a.11) there is a dispute between Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefutzai and Rabbi Hanina ben Antigonus.

Rabbi Akiva saw that there was blessing in him and gave him his daughter as a wife. He lived long, until the time of Rabbi, as in Shabbat 146a (compare [Shabbat 147a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.147a.10)): Yehoshua ben Kefosai, the son-in-law of Rabbi Akiva, said before him: ‘Rabbi, did Rabbi Akiva not impose liability for a sin-offering in this case?’ He replied: ‘Was Rabbi Akiva particular to this extent?’ Rabbi let down his cloak.

In [Yerushalmi Pesachim, chapter 6, halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.6.1.7), Rabbi Yoshia ben Kabsa said: ‘All my days I fled from authority. Now that I have entered it, anyone who comes and removes me—with this kettle I will come down on him.’
Something similar is said in [Menachot 109b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.109b.18) about Rabbi Yehoshua ben Perachya.[^1]

notes.text: Hyman’s Tosefta sources use variant spellings. The fuller treasury-of-Yavneh comparison quotes Numbers 19:19. Shabbat 147a has the two rhetorical questions and Rabbi letting down his cloak. The consulted Yerushalmi Pesachim gives Yehoshua ben Kabusai and “like this kettle,” where Hyman gives Yoshia and “with this kettle.” Menachot gives a parallel image in the name of Yehoshua ben Perachya.
